about: PDPA checklist for small businesses. Checked 11 Nov 2026 against Act 709 (reprint text), gazette P.U.(B) 522, the JPDP DBN and DPO guidelines (25 Feb 2025) and Commissioner's Circular No. 1/2026. Not legal advice. 'when' limits an item to businesses where it applies (see app/js/checklist.js).

items.q: Do you know whether the business must register with JPDP, and is it registered if required?
items.help: Required for the 13 classes (e.g. private clinics, accounting firms, registered private educational institutions), except PLTs. RM100–RM400 a year. Display the certificate at your premises.

items.q: Have you checked whether you need a Data Protection Officer, and appointed and registered one within 21 days if so?
items.help: Over 20,000 people, over 10,000 with sensitive or financial data, or regular and systematic monitoring. If not needed, keep a short note of why.

items.q: Is one named person responsible for personal data, with a backup?
items.help: Often the owner. Their name goes on the privacy notice and the breach plan.

items.q: Do you have a list of all the personal data you hold (whose, how many, where, who can see it, how long)?
items.help: The Personal data page in this app.

items.q: Do people get a written privacy notice in Malay and English when you collect their data?
items.help: Say what you collect, why, who you share it with, whether it's required, and how to contact you or ask for a copy.

items.q: Do you have consent (or another legal basis, such as a contract) for each use of personal data?
items.help: Collecting a phone number for an order isn't consent to send promotions.

items.q: Do you get explicit consent before collecting sensitive data?
items.help: Health, religious or similar beliefs, offences, biometrics, political opinions.

items.q: For children under 18, does consent come from a parent or guardian?
items.help: Includes permission to post photos or results.

items.q: Do marketing messages go only to people who opted in, and stop when someone asks?
items.help: A written request to stop direct marketing must get a written reply within 21 days.

items.q: Are there CCTV signs, and is footage viewing and retention limited?
items.help: Also record your reasoning on whether CCTV counts as systematic monitoring for the DPO rule.

items.q: Can people withdraw consent, and do you stop processing when they do?
items.help: Withdrawal is by written notice.

items.q: Do you only share personal data for the purpose people were told about?
items.help: No selling or passing on lists. No posting customer details in public groups.

items.q: Do you collect only what you need?
items.help: e.g. a tuition centre doesn't need parents' IC numbers to run a class.

items.q: Have you set how long each type of data is kept, and do you delete or shred it after?
items.help: Keep what other laws require (e.g. tax, medical records), then dispose of it.

items.q: Do you keep personal data accurate and up to date?
items.help: Fix wrong details when you learn of them.

items.q: Do you know if personal data is stored or sent outside Malaysia (e.g. cloud services), and have you checked the transfer rules?
items.help: The cross-border transfer rules changed on 1 April 2025. Check the current JPDP guidance.

items.q: Do you take practical steps to protect personal data (MFA, individual logins, updates, backups, encryption, locked storage)?
items.help: The toolkit controls and policies are these practical steps.

items.q: Can only the people who need it see each set of personal data?
items.help: Especially health, children's, ID and financial data.

items.q: Do suppliers, vendors and freelancers who process personal data for you have written terms to protect it?
items.help: Processors are bound by the Security Principle themselves since 1 April 2025, but you still need the contract terms.

items.q: Have staff been trained on handling personal data and spotting scams?
items.help: At hiring and yearly.

items.q: Can you give someone a copy of their data, in writing, within 21 days of asking?
items.help: Know where all their data is (the inventory) so you can find it.

items.q: Do you correct data within 21 days when someone shows it's wrong?
items.help: Tell them in writing what you corrected.

items.q: Do you keep a record of requests, notices and consents?
items.help: A simple log is enough.

items.q: Do you have a written breach plan (who does what, containment, deciding whether to notify, communication, review)?
items.help: The Breach plan page in this app generates one.

items.q: Does everyone know to report a suspected breach immediately?
items.help: The 72-hour clock starts when the business is told about or finds the breach.

items.q: Do you know when to notify JPDP (72 hours) and the affected people (7 days)?
items.help: JPDP: significant harm or more than 1,000 people. People: significant harm. Use the online form at pdp.gov.my or email dbnpdp@pdp.gov.my.

items.q: Do you keep a breach register, including breaches you didn't notify, for at least 2 years?
items.help: The Breach register page in this app.
